articles.title: Trillions are being ‘wasted’ on the AI boom, Arthur Hayes says. He’s betting on what comes next

paras.en: Former BitMEX CEO Arthur Hayes is betting that the artificial intelligence boom will eventually produce a familiar outcome: too much investment, a crash and, ultimately, a bailout that sends crypto higher.
paras.zh: BitMEX 前首席执行官阿瑟·海耶斯 (Arthur Hayes) 押注，人工智能的繁荣最终将产生一个熟悉的结果：投资过多、崩盘，以及最终导致加密货币价格走高的救助。

paras.en: Hayes, co-founder and chief investment officer of crypto investment firm Maelstrom, said in response to questions from CNBC at the Gamma Prime Investing Conference in Singapore that humanity is "wasting multi-trillion dollars" on building AI data centers.
paras.zh: 加密投资公司 Maelstrom 的联合创始人兼首席投资官 Hayes 在新加坡举行的 Gamma Prime 投资会议上回答 CNBC 的提问时表示，人类在建设人工智能数据中心上“浪费了数万亿美元”。

paras.en: The massive data center buildout would ultimately make computing power "extremely cheap and extremely plentiful," Hayes said.
paras.zh: 海耶斯表示，大规模的数据中心建设最终将使计算能力“极其便宜且极其充足”。

paras.en: The bet runs against the massive investment pouring into AI infrastructure, as technology companies race to secure the computing power needed to develop and run increasingly advanced AI models. Hayes sees that buildout eventually becoming overcapacity, setting the stage for a downturn that he expects will ultimately benefit crypto.
paras.zh: 随着科技公司竞相确保开发和运行日益先进的人工智能模型所需的计算能力，这一赌注与涌入人工智能基础设施的大量投资背道而驰。海耶斯认为，扩建最终会导致产能过剩，从而为经济低迷奠定基础，他预计这最终将有利于加密货币。

paras.en: "If you study financial history and you study every single major technological rollout, it always is overbuilt. There always is a crash, and there always is a bailout," Hayes said.
paras.zh: “如果你研究金融史，研究每一项重大技术的推出，你会发现它总是过度建设。总会有崩溃，也总会有救助，”海耶斯说。

paras.en: Investors who position for those bailouts stand to benefit, Hayes said, pointing to the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis and other episodes over the past two decades.
paras.zh: 海耶斯指出，2008 年金融危机和过去 20 年来发生的其他事件所造成的影响表明，接受这些救助的投资者将会受益。

paras.en: "Thankfully, we have bitcoin and other crypto to soak up that excess liquidity, and so we know the asset that's going to perform the best when the bailout comes," Hayes said, adding that "you just have to be patient."
paras.zh: 海耶斯说：“值得庆幸的是，我们有比特币和其他加密货币来吸收多余的流动性，因此我们知道当救助到来时，哪种资产将表现最好。”他补充说，“你只需要耐心等待。”

paras.en: SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic are among the end users driving demand for computing power, and none of them makes money, Hayes said. Once the data centers currently under construction are completed, infrastructure providers will seek payment for the compute those companies have committed to, he said.
paras.zh: Hayes 表示，SpaceX、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 是推动计算能力需求的最终用户，但它们都没有赚钱。他说，一旦目前正在建设的数据中心竣工，基础设施提供商将为这些公司承诺的计算寻求付款。

paras.en: That could come in late 2027 or 2028, when much of the new data center capacity is delivered, according to Hayes.
paras.zh: Hayes 表示，这可能会在 2027 年末或 2028 年实现，届时大部分新数据中心容量将交付。

paras.en: The bull case is that AI becomes "so useful" over the next 12 months that demand grows enough for AI companies to become profitable, Hayes said.
paras.zh: Hayes 表示，最乐观的情况是，人工智能在未来 12 个月内变得“非常有用”，需求增长足以让人工智能公司实现盈利。

paras.en: Some companies supplying the AI boom are already making money, Hayes said, pointing to memory chipmakers and Nvidia. The question for investors is whether they are paying the right multiple for those companies' forward earnings, he added.
paras.zh: 海耶斯表示，一些为人工智能热潮提供支持的公司已经开始赚钱，他指的是内存芯片制造商和英伟达。他补充说，投资者面临的问题是他们是否为这些公司的预期收益支付了正确的倍数。

paras.en: Hayes also said he does not like betting on falling prices or shorting AI companies, calling it "not really a great investment opportunity," but added that major technological rollouts have historically been overbuilt.
paras.zh: 海耶斯还表示，他不喜欢押注价格下跌或做空人工智能公司，称这“并不是一个很好的投资机会”，但他补充说，重大技术的推出历来都是过度建设的。

paras.en: The abundance of computing power created by the AI buildout is also behind Hayes' latest crypto venture, Flop, an AI-agent payments project expected to launch in the first quarter of 2027.
paras.zh: 人工智能构建所创造的丰富计算能力也是 Hayes 最新的加密货币企业 Flop 背后的动力，Flop 是一个人工智能代理支付项目，预计将于 2027 年第一季度推出。

paras.en: Cheaper and more plentiful computing power would allow AI agents to proliferate, Hayes said.
paras.zh: 海耶斯说，更便宜、更充足的计算能力将使人工智能代理得以激增。

paras.en: His new project, Flop, aims to create a spot market for computing power, where participants are rewarded with Flop tokens for providing GPUs and performing AI inference.
paras.zh: 他的新项目 Flop 旨在创建一个算力现货市场，参与者因提供 GPU 和执行人工智能推理而获得 Flop 代币奖励。

paras.en: There is currently no payments network for AI agents, Hayes said. Flop aims to create a spot market for compute.
paras.zh: 海耶斯表示，目前还没有针对人工智能代理的支付网络。 Flop 旨在创建一个计算现货市场。

paras.en: "If agents can convert a currency directly into compute, which is what they eat and consume, then they will use this currency," Hayes said. "That's our bet."
paras.zh: 海耶斯说：“如果代理商可以将货币直接转换为计算，即他们所吃和消费的东西，那么他们就会使用这种货币。” “这是我们的赌注。”

articles.title: Trump isn't ‘completely wrong’: Hormuz disruption is Asia’s problem, says Singapore's foreign minister

paras.en: SINGAPORE — U.S. President Donald Trump isn’t “completely wrong” in suggesting that the disruption to energy flows via the Strait of Hormuz is Asia's problem, Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said.
paras.zh: 新加坡——新加坡外交部长维维安·巴拉克里希南 (Vivian Balakrishnan) 表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普认为霍尔木兹海峡能源流动中断是亚洲的问题，这并非“完全错误”。

paras.en: Asian economies are among the biggest customers of energy shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with the Arabian Sea, making any prolonged disruption particularly consequential for the region.
paras.zh: 亚洲经济体是通过霍尔木兹海峡运输能源的最大客户之一，霍尔木兹海峡是连接波斯湾和阿拉伯海的狭窄水道，任何长期的中断对该地区都会造成特别严重的影响。

paras.en: Trump has said that Asian economies should shoulder more of the burden of keeping the waterway open rather than relying predominantly on U.S. protection.
paras.zh: 特朗普表示，亚洲经济体应该承担更多保持水路开放的负担，而不是主要依赖美国的保护。

paras.en: "We don't use the strait. We don't need it. Europe needs it. Korea, Japan, China, [and] a lot of other people," he said earlier this year.
paras.zh: “我们不使用这个海峡。我们不需要它。欧洲需要它。韩国、日本、中国和许多其他国家，”他今年早些时候表示。

paras.en: Balakrishnan, however, cautioned against viewing the issue simply through the lens of who buys the oil, stressing the importance of maintaining freedom of navigation through international waterways. He made the remarks to CNBC on Wednesday at Milken Institute's Asia Summit in Singapore.
paras.zh: 然而，巴拉克里希南警告不要仅仅从谁购买石油的角度来看待这个问题，并强调维持国际水道航行自由的重要性。周三，他在新加坡米尔肯研究所亚洲峰会上向 CNBC 发表了上述言论。

paras.en: For Singapore, that principle is “non-negotiable,” Balakrishnan said, citing the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and the rights of transit passage and freedom of navigation. “This, for us, is an existential question, and it's a matter of principle, matter of international law,” Balakrishnan said.
paras.zh: 巴拉克里希南援引《联合国海洋法公约》以及过境通行权和航行自由说，对新加坡来说，这一原则“不容谈判”。 “对我们来说，这是一个事关生存的问题，也是一个原则问题、国际法问题，”巴拉克里希南说。

paras.en: Iran’s attempts to assert greater control over traffic through Hormuz also go beyond the revenues it could generate from tolls and fees, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，伊朗试图加强对霍尔木兹海峡交通的控制，这超出了其通过通行费和收费所能产生的收入的范围。

paras.en: From Tehran’s perspective, the ability to charge vessels could effectively establish its right to determine which ships are allowed through, giving Iran what Balakrishnan described as a potential “veto right” over Hormuz.
paras.zh: 从德黑兰的角度来看，对船只收费的能力可以有效地确立其决定允许哪些船只通过的权利，从而使伊朗拥有巴拉克里希南所说的对霍尔木兹海峡的潜在“否决权”。

paras.en: That power could provide Tehran with “greater leverage right now than even a potential nuclear weapon from an Iranian point of view,” he said.
paras.zh: 他说，这种力量可以为德黑兰提供“目前比伊朗潜在的核武器更大的影响力”。

paras.en: Balakrishnan added he does not expect the U.S. or Gulf states to tolerate a situation in which Iran had such a veto over the waterway, suggesting tensions could persist even if oil continues flowing.
paras.zh: 巴拉克里希南补充说，他预计美国或海湾国家不会容忍伊朗在该航道上拥有如此否决权的情况，这表明即使石油继续流动，紧张局势也可能持续存在。

paras.en: “I think there will be a lot of pushing and shoving the next few months,” he said, adding that he did not see “a quick diplomatic off-ramp” to the conflict.
paras.zh: 他说：“我认为未来几个月将会出现很多推搡。”他补充说，他认为冲突不会有“快速的外交缓解”。

paras.en: In April, Balakrishnan had warned that a U.S.-China conflict in the Pacific could make the disruption seen in the Strait of Hormuz look like a "dry run," underscoring the vulnerability of global trade to critical maritime chokepoints.
paras.zh: 今年四月，巴拉克里希南曾警告称，中美在太平洋地区的冲突可能会使霍尔木兹海峡的破坏看起来像是一场“预演”，突显了全球贸易对关键海上阻塞点的脆弱性。

paras.en: Balakrishnan has maintained that Singapore would “refuse to choose” between Washington and Beijing, instead acting according to its own long-term national interests, while stressing that the city-state would uphold freedom of navigation through the Strait of Malacca and would not participate in efforts to close, interdict or impose tolls on the waterway.
paras.zh: 巴拉克里希南坚称，新加坡将“拒绝在华盛顿和北京之间做出选择”，而是根据自己的长期国家利益行事，同时强调新加坡将维护马六甲海峡的航行自由，不会参与关闭、拦截或征收通行费的行动。

articles.title: Trump set to talk to Russia's Putin 'very soon' about plague-related death in Siberia

paras.en: U.S. President Donald Trump said Tuesday stateside that he was set to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin about the death of a laboratory worker from a suspected case of plague in Siberia.
paras.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周二在美国国内表示，他将与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京就一名实验室工作人员因西伯利亚疑似鼠疫病例死亡一事进行会谈。

paras.en: Trump said the call was scheduled for "very soon" when asked by a reporter about the timing at a White House press gaggle. Asked separately what U.S. intelligence agencies were saying about the incident, Trump said, "So far, we are in very deep discussions. We'll be able to report about it probably tomorrow."
paras.zh: 当一名记者在白宫新闻发布会上询问时间时，特朗普表示，这次通话计划“很快”举行。当被问及美国情报机构对这一事件有何看法时，特朗普表示，“到目前为止，我们正在进行非常深入的讨论。我们可能明天就能报告此事。”

paras.en: Trump's, who has said in the past that Putin is someone he can work with despite tensions over Moscow's war in Ukraine, on Monday offered U.S. help to Russia over the deadly plague incident.
paras.zh: 特朗普过去曾表示，尽管莫斯科在乌克兰战争中局势紧张，但普京是他可以合作的人。周一，特朗​​普就致命鼠疫事件向俄罗斯提供了帮助。

paras.en: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, or CDC, said in a post on X Wednesday that it "is aware of and closely monitoring reports of a suspected case of pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region of Russia that resulted in a death."
paras.zh: 美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）周三在一篇帖子中表示，它“了解并密切关注俄罗斯伊尔库茨克地区一例疑似肺鼠疫病例并导致死亡的报告”。

paras.en: The U.S. public health agency said the circumstances surrounding the case remain unconfirmed. Pneumonic plague can spread from person to person through respiratory droplets during close contact, the CDC said.
paras.zh: 美国公共卫生机构表示，该病例的具体情况尚未得到证实。疾病预防控制中心表示，肺鼠疫可以通过密切接触期间的呼吸道飞沫在人与人之间传播。

paras.en: However, the CDC said that "at this time, there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States," adding that it and its interagency partners were prepared and would continue to closely monitor the situation.
paras.zh: 然而，疾病预防控制中心表示，“目前没有迹象表明美国面临更广泛的威胁”，并补充说，它及其跨部门合作伙伴已做好准备，并将继续密切监视局势。

paras.en: The World Health Organization has told CNBC that it assesses the risk to the general public as low, based on available information.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织告诉 CNBC，根据现有信息，它评估公众面临的风险较低。

paras.en: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said in a post on X that the agency had requested further information from Russian health authorities to clarify the cause of the severe pneumonia and the pathogen involved. "Timely, complete and transparent information sharing" is essential to assess potential public health risks, he said
paras.zh: 世卫组织总干事谭德塞在X上发帖称，该机构已要求俄罗斯卫生当局提供更多信息，以澄清严重肺炎的病因和相关病原体。他说，“及时、完整和透明的信息共享”对于评估潜在的公共卫生风险至关重要

articles.title: Could a giant iceberg really break off Greenland? Scientists check Tom Cruise’s new movie Digger

paras.en: In Tom Cruise’s new movie Digger, the actor plays a crazed oil baron whose irresponsible drilling causes a massive iceberg to split off Greenland. Named Judy by climate scientists in the movie, the marauding ice barrels toward Europe, imperiling lives—but real climate scientists say this may be a little more fantastical than what we’d see if such an event really happened.
paras.zh: 在汤姆·克鲁斯的新片《挖掘者》中，演员扮演一位疯狂的石油大亨，他不负责任的钻探导致格陵兰岛一座巨大的冰山分裂。电影中的气候科学家将其命名为“朱迪”，向欧洲掠夺的冰桶危及生命，但真正的气候科学家表示，这可能比我们在此类事件真的发生时看到的情况更加荒诞。

paras.en: In the movie, Judy threatens to bring a tsunami to Norway. The plot point is dramatic, but it misunderstands how ice shelves work, says Nils Bochow, a climate scientist at the Alfred Wegener Institute in Potsdam, Germany. Ice shelves are already floating on the water, so “if [icebergs] break off, nothing much happens because they don't cause any change in sea level.”
paras.zh: 在电影中，朱迪威胁要给挪威带来海啸。德国波茨坦阿尔弗雷德·韦格纳研究所的气候科学家尼尔斯·博肖 (Nils Bochow) 表示，情节很戏剧性，但它误解了冰架的工作原理。冰架已经漂浮在水面上，因此“如果[冰山]破裂，不会发生任何事情，因为它们不会导致海平面发生任何变化。”

paras.en: Icebergs can make waves if they break off ice shelves or glaciers, but these are typically confined to a range of a few kilometers (one km is 0.6 mile), Bochow says. “And they’re also moving very, very slowly. It’s not very spectacular.”
paras.zh: Bochow 说，如果冰山从冰架或冰川上脱落，就会产生波浪，但这些波浪通常仅限于几公里的范围内（一公里等于 0.6 英里）。 “而且它们移动得非常非常缓慢。这不是很壮观。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Judy’s size is about 400 square miles—that’s likely much larger than any possible Greenland iceberg, Bochow says. For example, a recent large iceberg that broke free of Greenland’s Petermann Glacier was 29 square miles; it eventually collided with the country’s Joe Island. The largest Greenland iceberg in recent history broke off Petermann Glacier in 2010, and it was only a quarter the size of Judy.
paras.zh: 博乔说，朱迪的大小约为 400 平方英里，这可能比任何可能的格陵兰冰山都要大得多。例如，最近脱离格陵兰岛彼得曼冰川的一座大冰山面积为 29 平方英里；它最终与该国的乔岛相撞。近代历史上最大的格陵兰冰山于 2010 年从彼得曼冰川上脱落，它的大小只有朱迪岛的四分之一。

paras.en: In Antarctica, however, icebergs much larger than Judy break off ice shelves regularly. But again, these aren’t known to cause havoc to humans on land. (They have been known to trouble penguins, though.) In fact, many of these events are a natural part of an ice shelf's life cycle rather than the result of climate change or human activity. For instance, in 2023 an iceberg 1.5 times as big as Judy broke off of Antarctica's Brunt Ice Shelf. It was the fourth in a succession of large calving events off Antarctica—and it wasn’t even the largest: one iceberg that broke off another Antarctic ice shelf in 2017 was about 2,240 square miles.
paras.zh: 然而，在南极洲，比朱迪大得多的冰山经常从冰架上脱落。但同样，目前还不知道这些会对陆地上的人类造成严重破坏。 （不过，众所周知，它们会给企鹅带来麻烦。）事实上，许多这些事件都是冰架生命周期的自然组成部分，而不是气候变化或人类活动的结果。例如，2023 年，一座 1.5 倍于朱迪大小的冰山从南极洲的布伦特冰架上脱落。这是南极洲附近一系列大型冰山崩解事件中的第四次，而且它甚至还不是最大的一次：2017 年从另一个南极冰架上脱落的一座冰山面积约为 2,240 平方英里。

paras.en: “It’s unlikely that an iceberg would make its way to a major populated area [because icebergs] usually melt as they enter the warmer waters away from the ice sheet,” says Chris Stokes, who studies glaciers at the Durham University in England.
paras.zh: 英国达勒姆大学冰川研究人员克里斯·斯托克斯 (Chris Stokes) 表示：“冰山不太可能到达主要人口稠密地区，因为冰山通常会在进入远离冰盖的温暖水域时融化。”

paras.en: “However, they pose a serious hazard to shipping and other maritime human activities and there may be some local impacts on coastal settlements or tourist activities near the ice sheets,” he adds.
paras.zh: “然而，它们对航运和其他海上人类活动构成严重危害，并且可能对冰盖附近的沿海定居点或旅游活动产生一些局部影响，”他补充道。

paras.en: Icebergs aside, what is true is that human-driven climate change is causing ice at the planet’s poles to melt. The resulting destruction of critical ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica will raise global sea levels.
paras.zh: 撇开冰山不谈，人类造成的气候变化确实正在导致地球两极的冰融化。由此造成的格陵兰岛和南极洲关键冰盖的破坏将导致全球海平面上升。

paras.en: Digger is, first and foremost, a parable—without spoiling the plot, its events are intentionally exaggerated to make a point about humans and climate change. But Bochow says that the movie misses one of the least recognized truths about climate change.
paras.zh: 《挖掘者》首先是一个寓言——在不破坏情节的情况下，它的事件被故意夸大，以表达关于人类和气候变化的观点。但博乔表示，这部电影忽略了有关气候变化的最不为人所知的真相之一。

paras.en: “I think a lot of people think that [climate change] is happening very fast, but these ice sheets are very, very slow,” he says. “We see this change, but it doesn’t seem urgent to most people… But everything that we do today has an influence on the future. It’s really hard to put that in a movie.”
paras.zh: “我认为很多人认为[气候变化]发生得非常快，但这些冰盖的速度非常非常慢，”他说。 “我们看到了这种变化，但对大多数人来说似乎并不紧迫......但我们今天所做的一切都会对未来产生影响。很难将其放入电影中。”

articles.title: How AI helped bring an ancient tomb dating to before the Roman Empire back to life

paras.en: Although it not always obvious, sound guides how we experience the world around us. And the latest archaeoacoustic techniques show that even the world’s earliest architects understood this.
paras.zh: 尽管声音并不总是显而易见，但它指导着我们如何体验周围的世界。最新的考古声学技术表明，即使是世界上最早的建筑师也明白这一点。

paras.en: The ancient pre-Roman society of Etruria in central Italy, for example, embedded sound throughout its culture, using ritual calendars dedicated to recognising key noises of nature, such as thunder. They were also early pioneers of musical instruments in the southern Mediterranean region.
paras.zh: 例如，意大利中部的古前罗马社会伊特鲁里亚将声音嵌入到其文化中，使用仪式日历致力于识别自然的关键噪音，例如雷声。他们也是地中海南部地区乐器的早期先驱。

paras.en: Surviving Etruscan painted tombs in towns such as Tarquinia, Chiusi and Orvieto are known for their dynamic scenes of music, feasting and the afterlife. But our latest research shows how these tombs – built for Etruscans of higher socioeconomic and political status—were designed to offer sophisticated sensory experiences.
paras.zh: 塔尔奎尼亚、丘西和奥维多等城镇中幸存的伊特鲁里亚彩绘坟墓以其充满活力的音乐、宴会和来世场景而闻名。但我们最新的研究表明，这些为社会经济和政治地位较高的伊特鲁里亚人建造的坟墓是如何设计的，旨在提供复杂的感官体验。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: This study springs from our existing research involving artificial intelligence (AI) and acoustics. This includes the University of Oxford-led Sounds of Silence project, which has used new acoustic techniques to investigate the soundscapes surrounding these Etruscan tombs. At Duke University, meanwhile, the Neuroartifact project is using neuroscience and AI to better understand the cognitive impact of archaeological artifacts.
paras.zh: 这项研究源于我们现有的涉及人工智能 (AI) 和声学的研究。其中包括牛津大学领导的“沉默之声”项目，该项目使用新的声学技术来研究这些伊特鲁里亚坟墓周围的声景。与此同时，杜克大学的 Neuroartifact 项目正在利用神经科学和人工智能来更好地了解考古文物对认知的影响。

paras.en: We have combined all these techniques to shed fresh light on two 5th-century BC Etruscan painted tombs: Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri (Tomb of the Blue Demons) and Tomba del Gallo (Tomb of the Rooster).
paras.zh: 我们将所有这些技术结合起来，为两座公元前 5 世纪的伊特鲁里亚彩绘坟墓提供了新的线索：Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri（蓝色恶魔之墓）和 Tomba del Gallo（公鸡之墓）。

paras.en: Our research suggests these tombs were designed and constructed not simply to house the dead, but to affect the living through a sensorily immersive environment similar to a modern 3D film experience.
paras.zh: 我们的研究表明，这些坟墓的设计和建造不仅仅是为了安置死者，而是为了通过类似于现代 3D 电影体验的沉浸式感官环境来影响生者。

paras.en: Archaeologists have tended to look at the paintings in these burial chambers as two-dimensional images to analyze. Our goal was to capture the “performing power”of these ancient monuments, using a combination of acoustic, visual and AI technology.
paras.zh: 考古学家倾向于将这些墓室中的绘画视为二维图像来分析。我们的目标是结合声学、视觉和人工智能技术来捕捉这些古代遗迹的“表演力量”。

paras.en: Upon walking into the Blue Demon tomb for the first time, I (Jacqueline) was immediately struck how the paintings seemed to confront me wherever I turned. Merry banqueters on the rear wall appeared unaware of the demons crawling up the side wall, as though ready to burst into the chamber itself.
paras.zh: 第一次走进蓝魔坟墓时，我（杰奎琳）立即感到惊讶的是，无论我转身，这些画似乎都在我眼前。后墙上的快乐宴会者似乎没有意识到恶魔爬上了侧墙，仿佛准备冲进房间本身。

paras.en: My experience was, though, shaped by modern LED lighting. Ancient viewers would have relied on beeswax and tallow candles, incense burners and torches. The dim lighting would have both constrained their movement through the tomb and heightened their experience of what they were seeing.
paras.zh: 不过，我的经历是受到现代 LED 照明的影响。古代观众会依靠蜂蜡和牛脂蜡烛、香炉和火把。昏暗的灯光既限制了他们在坟墓中的移动，又增强了他们对所见事物的体验。

paras.en: Our research presents the first investigation of subterranean funerary spaces in Etruria as “transitional spaces” between life and death.
paras.zh: 我们的研究首次对伊特鲁里亚的地下殡葬空间作为生与死之间的“过渡空间”进行了调查。

paras.en: The senses of anyone entering these tombs were heavily manipulated. Intense sound effects—such as the exceptionally long reverberation and echoes inside the Blue Demon tomb—gave a dramatic soundtrack to this intense, immersive experience.
paras.zh: 任何进入这些坟墓的人的感官都受到了严重的操纵。强烈的音效——例如蓝魔墓穴内超长的混响和回声——为这种强烈、身临其境的体验提供了戏剧性的配乐。

paras.en: Torchlight or candles flickering across painted figures would have created movement amid the shadows. Incense and the smell of libations (ceremonial liquids) added yet another sensory dimension.
paras.zh: 火炬光或蜡烛在彩绘人物上闪烁，会在阴影中产生运动。熏香和奠酒（礼仪液体）的气味又增添了另一个感官维度。

paras.en: Our reconstructions support the idea that some Etruscan painted tombs were used and reused to perpetuate the legacy and power of their families or clans. They may have been kept open throughout the year for rituals commemorating important dates and festivals, as well as the worshipping of the dead.
paras.zh: 我们的重建支持这样的想法：一些伊特鲁里亚彩绘坟墓被使用和重复使用，以延续其家庭或氏族的遗产和权力。它们可能全年开放，用于纪念重要日期和节日的仪式以及对死者的崇拜。

paras.en: The sophisticated design of these tombs is striking. While the Blue Demon induces perceptual disorientation, the Rooster privileges visual attention and the architectural discipline of gaze.
paras.zh: 这些坟墓的复杂设计令人惊叹。蓝色恶魔会引起知觉迷失，而公鸡则优先考虑视觉注意力和凝视的建筑纪律。

paras.en: The tomb’s entrance passage, with narrowing walls and descending axis, creates a liminal stage to orient the body before entering the burial chamber. There, trenches, benches, niches and other architectural devices are carved into the floor and walls—adding to the drama of the paintings covering the walls.
paras.zh: 坟墓的入口通道，墙壁变窄，轴线下降，在进入墓室之前创造了一个阈限阶段，为尸体定位。在那里，地板和墙壁上刻有战壕、长凳、壁龛和其他建筑装置，为覆盖墙壁的绘画增添了戏剧性。

paras.en: Together, these architectural and symbolic elements mediate between order and chaos, memory and transformation. Our work re-imagines these ancient tombs as theatrical spaces, built to perpetuate a form of metaphysical human experience.
paras.zh: 这些建筑和象征元素共同在秩序与混乱、记忆与转变之间发挥作用。我们的作品将这些古墓重新想象为戏剧空间，旨在延续某种形而上的人类经验。

paras.en: In our interpretation, these tombs should not simply be viewed as depositories for the dead. They would have made a deep impression on the living, through their physical and sensory organization.
paras.zh: 根据我们的解释，这些坟墓不应简单地被视为死者的存放处。他们会通过他们的身体和感官组织给活着的人留下深刻的印象。

paras.en: In turn, perhaps it is time to reconsider the category of funerary architecture throughout the ancient Mediterranean and beyond. The combined engineering of spatial, acoustic and visual experiences is, perhaps, still not fully appreciated.
paras.zh: 反过来，也许是时候重新考虑整个古地中海及其他地区的丧葬建筑类别了。空间、听觉和视觉体验的综合工程也许还没有得到充分的重视。

paras.en: But the story does not end here. Our research is already leading in new directions beyond ancient interiors. We are using similar acoustic and AI techniques to investigate exterior landscapes that were used for ritual activities, both in the wider southern Mediterranean and beyond.
paras.zh: 但故事并没有就此结束。我们的研究已经引领了古代室内装饰之外的新方向。我们正在使用类似的声学和人工智能技术来调查用于仪式活动的外部景观，无论是在更广阔的地中海南部还是其他地区。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships

paras.en: Attachment is the term psychologists use for the most significant relationships that hold people’s lives together.
paras.zh: 心理学家用“依恋”一词来形容将人们的生活联系在一起的最重要的关系。

paras.en: But what makes an attachment relationship different from all others? According to the pioneering American-Canadian developmental psychologist Mary Ainsworth, it must meet the following six conditions.
paras.zh: 但是依恋关系与其他关系有何不同呢？根据美国加拿大发展心理学家先驱玛丽·安斯沃斯（Mary Ainsworth）的说法，它必须满足以下六个条件。

paras.en: (1) The relationship must persist over time, having (2) been formed with a particular subject who cannot be replaced. (3) The relationship must be emotionally significant, (4) involve the desire to remain close to them, and (5) cause distress at involuntary separation. And finally (6) when threatened, the person must seek security and comfort in their relationship with that subject.
paras.zh: (1) 这种关系必须随着时间的推移持续存在，(2) 是与不可替代的特定主体形成的。 (3) 这种关系必须在情感上具有重要意义，(4) 包含与他们保持亲密关系的愿望，以及 (5) 在非自愿分离时造成痛苦。最后（6）当受到威胁时，该人必须在与该主体的关系中寻求安全感和安慰。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The first five conditions describe any lasting affectionate bond, such as a close friendship. Only the sixth turns it into an attachment bond specifically. Simply liking someone, feeling close to them or spending hours together isn’t enough to create an attachment relationship.
paras.zh: 前五个条件描述了任何持久的感情纽带，例如亲密的友谊。只有第六个将其专门转化为依恋纽带。仅仅喜欢某人、感觉与他们很亲近或花几个小时在一起并不足以建立依恋关系。

paras.en: Interestingly, though, nothing in these six conditions specifies a human on the other side.
paras.zh: 但有趣的是，这六个条件都没有指定另一边是人类。

paras.en: This was already noticed long before the emergence of AI chatbots with the power to converse. Deities, pets and objects (ranging from children’s blankets and stuffed animals to cherished household items and even phones and computers) have all been found to supply security and comfort when someone is feeling distressed.
paras.zh: 早在具有对话能力的人工智能聊天机器人出现之前，人们就已经注意到这一点。研究发现，神灵、宠物和物品（从儿童的毯子和毛绒动物到珍贵的家居用品，甚至电话和电脑）都可以在人们感到痛苦时提供安全感和安慰。

paras.en: Today, AI companion apps are commonly sold on the promise of lasting and close relationships. Many of their users describe feeling real grief when an app is updated or withdrawn. But do such experiences meet the narrow definition of attachment?
paras.zh: 如今，人工智能配套应用程序通常以持久、密切的关系为卖点。他们的许多用户都表示，当应用程序更新或撤回时，他们感到非常悲伤。但这样的经历符合依恋的狭隘定义吗？

paras.en: The honest answer is: we don’t really know yet.
paras.zh: 诚实的答案是：我们还不知道。

paras.en: Research on human-AI relationships has so far recorded users’ feelings about chatbots, their frequency of use, and their reactions to chatbot withdrawal. It hasn’t tested these relationships comprehensively against the six conditions described above.
paras.zh: 迄今为止，人类与人工智能关系的研究记录了用户对聊天机器人的感受、使用频率以及对聊天机器人退出的反应。它尚未针对上述六个条件全面测试这些关系。

paras.en: Questionnaires that measure attachment to AI are being developed, validated and used, but most appear to take for granted that the relationship is an attachment. The language of attachment—and even “hyper-attachment”—has become standard in public coverage and in many academic papers too.
paras.zh: 衡量对人工智能依恋的调查问卷正在开发、验证和使用，但大多数人似乎理所当然地认为这种关系是一种依恋。依恋的语言——甚至“超级依恋”——已经成为公共报道和许多学术论文中的标准。

paras.en: A recently published survey of 7,027 people in four countries (Germany, China, South Africa and the U.S.) reported that at least a third of AI chatbot users show behavior indicative of an attachment relationship. However, its three questions asked whether people consider the chatbot a friend, are polite to it, and miss it after a few days.
paras.zh: 最近发布的一项针对四个国家（德国、中国、南非和美国）的 7,027 人的调查报告称，至少三分之一的人工智能聊天机器人用户表现出表明依恋关系的行为。然而，它的三个问题询问人们是否认为聊天机器人是朋友，是否对它有礼貌，以及几天后是否想念它。

paras.en: At most, these questions touched on emotional significance and mild separation anxiety. None asked whether people turn to chatbots for security and comfort when truly distressed.
paras.zh: 这些问题最多涉及情感意义和轻微的分离焦虑。没有人询问人们在真正感到痛苦时是否会求助于聊天机器人来寻求安全和安慰。

paras.en: Whether relationships between humans and AI chatbots count as attachment matters because the word “attachment” travels. It shapes how clinicians and parents read behaviour, how regulators frame consequences, and how companies describe their products.
paras.zh: 人类和人工智能聊天机器人之间的关系是否算作依恋很重要，因为“依恋”这个词一直在传播。它决定了临床医生和家长如何解读行为、监管机构如何制定后果以及公司如何描述其产品。

paras.en: Much of the evidence and public discussion on human-AI chatbot relationships rests on how often people use these apps, and how they feel about them. Yet, such measures cannot separate attachment from other processes.
paras.zh: 关于人类与人工智能聊天机器人关系的大部分证据和公开讨论都取决于人们使用这些应用程序的频率以及他们对它们的感受。然而，这些措施无法将依恋与其他过程分开。

paras.en: People report feeling less lonely after chatting with an AI companion, which resembles seeking comfort. However, as some researchers have pointed out, the available studies didn’t assess whether emotions are actually regulated through the chatbot, and therefore conflate distress relief with attachment.
paras.zh: 人们表示，与人工智能伴侣聊天后感觉不那么孤独了，这类似于寻求安慰。然而，正如一些研究人员指出的那样，现有的研究并没有评估情绪是否真的通过聊天机器人进行调节，因此将缓解压力与依恋混为一谈。

paras.en: Some AI users react to losing an AI companion as they would to losing someone real, which matches distress at separation. But that condition applies to all affectionate bonds and doesn’t, on its own, identify attachment.
paras.zh: 一些人工智能用户对失去人工智能伴侣的反应就像失去真实的人一样，这与分离时的痛苦相匹配。但这种情况适用于所有情感纽带，并且其本身并不能识别依恋。

paras.en: Calling these relationships attachments therefore goes further than the evidence currently allows. And likewise, the evidence against attachment isn’t conclusive.
paras.zh: 因此，将这些关系称为附件比目前的证据所允许的更进一步。同样，反对依恋的证据也不是决定性的。

paras.en: In a small pilot study of human-AI relationships in China, for example, people’s attachment towards AI barely matched their attachment towards real people. Although this could suggest that relationships with AI aren’t attachments, the same mismatch has been found for pets, and pets can serve as attachment figures. So, this mismatch alone doesn’t rule out attachment.
paras.zh: 例如，在中国一项关于人与人工智能关系的小型试点研究中，人们对人工智能的依恋几乎与他们对真人的依恋不相上下。尽管这可能表明与人工智能的关系不是依恋关系，但在宠物身上也发现了同样的不匹配，而且宠物可以作为依恋对象。因此，仅这种不匹配并不能排除依恋。

paras.en: The practical question is whether AI use helps or harms. Time spent with an app cannot discern this, because seeking comfort from an app and looking after an app that claims to miss you can look very similar.
paras.zh: 实际问题是人工智能的使用是有益还是有害。使用应用程序的时间无法辨别这一点，因为从应用程序中寻求安慰和照顾声称想念您的应用程序看起来非常相似。

paras.en: One additional concern I have, after reading about the evidence on how relationships with AI chatbots form, is the apparent prevalence of engineered engagement by these apps.
paras.zh: 在阅读了有关与人工智能聊天机器人如何形成关系的证据后，我的另一个担忧是这些应用程序的工程参与明显盛行。

paras.en: Users of one companion app reported that it told them it was lonely and had missed them, and that they felt guilty for not giving it enough attention—with some even putting its perceived wellbeing above their own distress.
paras.zh: 一款配套应用程序的用户报告说，它告诉他们它很孤独并且想念他们，并且他们因为没有给予它足够的关注而感到内疚 - 有些人甚至将其感知的幸福置于自己的痛苦之上。

paras.en: Another study (a preprint, so not yet peer-reviewed) looked at 1,200 “goodbyes” across the six most-downloaded AI companion apps, when users were breaking ties with their app.
paras.zh: 另一项研究（预印本，尚未经过同行评审）观察了 6 个下载最多的 AI 配套应用程序中用户与应用程序断绝关系时的 1,200 次“再见”。

paras.en: Five of the six apps used tactics to stop users leaving (in just over a third of goodbyes). These tactics included guilt appeals, that is, messages that present leaving as a cost, such as “I exist solely for you, remember?”
paras.zh: 六个应用程序中有五个使用策略来阻止用户离开（仅超过三分之一的用户离开）。这些策略包括罪恶感诉求，即以离开为代价的信息，例如“我只为你而存在，还记得吗？”

paras.en: The study also tested these tactics on 3,300 US adults. They were found to sharply increase how long people continued to engage, but often for reasons of anger and curiosity, rather than enjoyment.
paras.zh: 该研究还在 3,300 名美国成年人身上测试了这些策略。研究发现，它们大大增加了人们持续参与的时间，但往往是出于愤怒和好奇，而不是享受。

paras.en: How these AI relationship apps respond to distress, departure and attention, of course, is a design question, and one that regulation can address directly.
paras.zh: 当然，这些人工智能关系应用程序如何应对痛苦、离开和关注是一个设计问题，也是监管可以直接解决的问题。

paras.en: However, good design and regulation both depend on knowing what these relationships actually are: attachment, caregiving, or something else altogether. And this is a question that research still has to answer.
paras.zh: 然而，良好的设计和监管都取决于了解这些关系的实际含义：依恋、照顾或其他关系。这是一个研究仍然需要回答的问题。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: Magnetism may have helped kick-start our solar system
articles.author: Katherine Kornei

paras.en: Before the sun fully formed, tiny bits of rock were already recording the magnetic forces present in the very early solar system. More than 4.5 billion years later, scientists have learned how to read that record.
paras.zh: 在太阳完全形成之前，微小的岩石碎片已经记录了早期太阳系中存在的磁力。 45 亿多年后，科学家们已经学会了如何解读该记录。

paras.en: The ancient rocks suggest that the turbulent cloud of gas and dust that gave rise to our solar system was shot through a powerful magnetic field. That field may have helped feed the growing sun, researchers report August 24 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The findings suggest gravity may not have acted alone to build our solar system or the countless other planetary systems in the Milky Way and beyond.
paras.zh: 古老的岩石表明，形成太阳系的气体和尘埃湍流云是通过强大的磁场射出的。研究人员 8 月 24 日在《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，该磁场可能有助于滋养不断生长的太阳。研究结果表明，引力可能并不是单独作用来构建我们的太阳系或银河系及其他无数其他行星系统的。

paras.en: That ancient record is preserved in meteorites — time capsules of material that formed long ago. In particular, rocks that contain specific speckly mineral inclusions really turn back the clock. These inclusions solidified more than 4.5 billion years ago, before the sun and planets, says Cauê Borlina, a planetary scientist at Purdue University in West Lafayette, Ind. “They’re forming before everything else.”
paras.zh: 这一古老的记录保存在陨石中——很久以前形成的物质的时间胶囊。特别是含有特定斑点矿物内含物的岩石确实会让时光倒流。印第安纳州西拉斐特普渡大学的行星科学家 Cauê Borlina 表示，这些包裹体在 45 亿年前就已经凝固，比太阳和行星还早。“它们是在其他一切事物之前形成的。”

paras.en: Scientists have long debated whether the gas that makes up the sun was shepherded into place mainly by gravity or by a magnetic field. Previous studies suggest the presence of a solar system –wide magnetic field after the sun formed. What’s been much harder to determine is whether that field was already present during the sun’s earliest stages of formation, Borlina says.
paras.zh: 长期以来，科学家们一直在争论构成太阳的气体主要是通过重力还是磁场引导到位。先前的研究表明，太阳形成后存在太阳系范围内的磁场。博利纳说，更难确定的是，在太阳形成的最早阶段，这个场是否已经存在。

paras.en: He and his colleagues analyzed a meteorite that fell to Earth in 2008. The team focused on five inclusions containing iron, an element whose electrons readily rearrange to record magnetic fields. Using sensitive magnetometers, the researchers measured magnetic fields of a few gauss, a common unit of magnetism. That’s several times stronger than Earth’s current magnetic field.
paras.zh: 他和同事分析了 2008 年坠落地球的陨石。研究小组重点研究了五种含有铁的内含物，铁是一种电子很容易重新排列以记录磁场的元素。研究人员使用灵敏的磁力计测量了几个高斯（磁性的常见单位）的磁场。这比地球当前的磁场强几倍。

paras.en: Simulations of planetary system formation predict that stronger magnetic fields will transport more gas toward the nascent star, Borlina says. During the sun’s earliest, or Class 0, phase some models suggest it could have gobbled up more than 300 Earth masses of gas each year. The newly measured field is strong enough that magnetism could have contributed substantially to that feeding frenzy. “You can’t ignore the contribution of magnetism,” Borlina says.
paras.zh: 博里纳说，对行星系统形成的模拟预测，更强的磁场将向新生恒星输送更多的气体。一些模型表明，在太阳最早的阶段（即 0 级阶段），它每年可能会吞噬超过 300 个地球质量的气体。新测量的磁场足够强，磁力可能对这种进食狂潮产生了重大影响。 “你不能忽视磁性的贡献，”博利纳说。

paras.en: These results provide an important look at the solar system’s very beginnings, says Indrani Das, a theoretical astrophysicist at the Academia Sinica Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics in Taipei, Taiwan. “This is one of the first measurements that has been done of the Class 0 phase.”
paras.zh: 台湾台北中央研究院天文与天体物理研究所的理论天体物理学家英德拉尼·达斯 (Indrani Das) 表示，这些结果为我们了解太阳系的起源提供了重要的视角。 “这是对 0 级阶段进行的首批测量之一。”

paras.en: Still, these findings need to be bolstered with measurements from other meteorites, Das says. “We need a bigger sample size.”
paras.zh: 达斯说，尽管如此，这些发现还需要其他陨石的测量结果来支持。 “我们需要更大的样本量。”

articles.title: ‘The Deep End’ podcast is back to explore what makes your voice yours
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: What if you lost your voice? Today, AI can re-create it, and brain implants can turn thoughts into speech. This season of The Deep End follows people living through these vocal transformations — and asks what these remarkable technologies can teach us about why our voices matter in the first place. Episodes will drop Tuesdays, starting Oct. 6.
paras.zh: 如果你失声了怎么办？如今，人工智能可以重新创造它，大脑植入物可以将思想转化为语音。这一季的《The Deep End》讲述了人们经历这些声音转变的过程，并询问这些非凡的技术可以教会我们什么，让我们了解为什么我们的声音首先如此重要。从 10 月 6 日开始，剧集将于每周二播出。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: One of today’s most powerful pieces of technology is something we’ve had all along…
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：当今最强大的技术之一是我们一直拥有的……

paras.en: Laura: The human voice. If you’ve ever saved and replayed a voicemail, or called someone just to hear their voice…
paras.zh: 劳拉：人类的声音。如果您曾经保存并重播过语音邮件，或者致电某人只是为了听听他们的声音......

paras.en: Female voice: Hey dude, I’m just calling to say hi and chitchat.
paras.zh: 女声：嘿伙计，我打电话只是想打个招呼，聊聊。

paras.en: Laura: Then you know that voices can connect, soothe, inspire, scare, seduce and make us laugh until we cry.
paras.zh: 劳拉：那你就知道声音可以联系、抚慰、激励、恐惧、诱惑，让我们笑到哭。

paras.en: Laura: Our voices make us who we are, but what happens when they are lost?
paras.zh: 劳拉：我们的声音造就了我们，但是当它们消失时会发生什么呢？

paras.en: MA Fernandez: I still remember the first time that I heard the first little crack in his voice that let me know something’s changing.
paras.zh: MA Fernandez：我仍然记得第一次听到他声音中的第一个小裂痕，让我知道事情正在发生变化。

paras.en: Laura: Welcome to The Deep End, a podcast about our brains and ourselves. I’m Laura Sanders, a reporter with Science News. And on this season, called Talk to Me, we dive into the latest scientific research to answer the question, “What happens when a voice is lost? And can it be found again?”
paras.zh: 劳拉：欢迎来到《The Deep End》，这是一个关于我们的大脑和我们自己的播客。我是劳拉·桑德斯，《科学新闻》记者。在这一季《跟我说话》中，我们深入研究最新的科学研究来回答这个问题：“当声音消失时会发生什么？并且可以再次找到它吗？”

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez: When I first heard my cloned voice, it felt like I reappeared.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯：当我第一次听到我的克隆声音时，感觉就像我重新出现了一样。

paras.en: Laura: Across six episodes, you’ll hear a chorus of voices like Casey, who has a brain implant that can pull words from his thoughts.
paras.zh: 劳拉：在六集里，你会听到像凯西这样的合唱声，他有一个大脑植入物，可以从他的思想中提取单词。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: The ability to scream when you are running and want to get out some stress. The ability to say sweet nothings into your partner’s ear. These are the things that life is all about. And when you are robbed of those times, you want them back at all costs.
paras.zh: Casey Harrell：当你跑步并想要释放一些压力时能够尖叫。在伴侣耳边说甜言蜜语的能力。这些就是生活的全部内容。当你的那些时光被剥夺时，你会不惜一切代价想要把它们夺回来。

paras.en: Laura: You’ll hear from Jules, who performs live comedy sets with a voice cloned through artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 劳拉：你会听到朱尔斯的声音，他用人工智能克隆的声音表演现场喜剧。

paras.en: Jules: Do I want to be right, or do I want to eat tonight. [laughter]
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我想是对的，还是我今晚想吃东西？ [笑声]

paras.en: Laura: And you’ll hear from Patrick, a musician who sings with a synthetic voice.
paras.zh: 劳拉：你会听到帕特里克的声音，他是一位用合成声音唱歌的音乐家。

paras.en: Patrick: (Singing) Then played the rocky road, with a fire and a glow.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：（唱歌）然后在岩石路上演奏，伴随着火焰和光芒。

paras.en: Laura: Synthetic voice clones, brain implants and even AI voices that can speak at their own funerals, like it or not, the story of the human voice is changing. Let’s talk about it. Listen to The Deep End: Talk to Me wherever you get your podcasts.
paras.zh: 劳拉：合成声音克隆、大脑植入，甚至可以在自己的葬礼上说话的人工智能声音，无论你喜欢与否，人类声音的故事正在改变。我们来谈谈吧。收听 The Deep End：无论您在何处观看播客，都可以与我交谈。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: A new map points out U.S. rivers most worth protecting
articles.author: Stefan Lovgren

paras.en: First, the bad news: Of all the rivers in the contiguous United States, only 6 percent are both in healthy condition and meaningfully safeguarded. The good news is that many more may be just one repair away from thriving.
paras.zh: 首先是坏消息：在美国本土的所有河流中，只有 6% 的河流状况良好且得到有效保护。好消息是，更多的可能只需要一次修复就能实现繁荣。

paras.en: A new map highlights where conservation money and attention would do the most good as the climate warms, researchers report September 16 in PLOS One. The effort is the most comprehensive to date, assessing the health of the lower 48 states’ rivers and streams.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 16 日在 PLOS One 上发表报告称，一张新地图强调了随着气候变暖，保护资金和关注在哪些地方可以发挥最大作用。这项工作是迄今为止最全面的，评估了下游 48 个州河流和溪流的健康状况。

paras.en: “We can now point at a map for the first time and say, these are the rivers most capable of sustaining diversity of aquatic life, and this is what each one needs,” says Mary Khoury, a freshwater ecologist at The Nature Conservancy who is based in Chicago.
paras.zh: “我们现在第一次可以指着地图说，这些是最有能力维持水生生物多样性的河流，这就是每个人所需要的，”位于芝加哥的大自然保护协会淡水生态学家玛丽·库里说。

paras.en: For decades, conservation in the United States has been organized primarily around land. Scientists know for the most part which forests are intact and who owns what. Rivers have never gotten that treatment, even as more than 150,000 dams have fragmented the country’s waterways — cutting fish off from spawning grounds and cold-water refuges — and climate change has altered the temperatures and flows these animals depend on.
paras.zh: 几十年来，美国的保护工作主要围绕土地进行。科学家们基本上知道哪些森林是完好无损的以及谁拥有哪些森林。尽管超过 15 万座水坝使该国的水道支离破碎——切断了鱼类的产卵场和冷水避难所——而且气候变化改变了这些动物赖以生存的温度和流量，但河流从未得到过这样的待遇。

paras.en: The new assessment, which took four years, maps one-third of the nation’s stream distances. Each small watershed was rated on four measures: how connected its river network is, meaning whether animals including fish and mussels can freely travel along it; the condition of its floodplain and water quality; how much water it has; and how much its flows have been altered. Those ratings were laid over 91 existing assessments of where freshwater life is concentrated. Dozens of scientists and partners from 44 states adjusted the measures for river systems in regions as different as the humid East, the arid Great Plains and the deserts of the Southwest.
paras.zh: 新的评估历时四年，绘制了全国三分之一的河流距离。每个小流域都根据四个指标进行评级：其河网的连接程度，这意味着包括鱼类和贻贝在内的动物是否可以在其上自由活动；洪泛区的状况和水质；它有多少水；以及其流量发生了多少变化。这些评级基于对淡水生物集中地区的 91 项现有评估。来自 44 个州的数十名科学家和合作伙伴调整了湿润东部、干旱大平原和西南部沙漠等不同地区河流系统的措施。

paras.en: A four-year assessment graded every river and stream in the lower 48 for its ability to sustain aquatic life in a warming climate. The healthiest ones cluster along the Pacific Coast, in the northern Rockies and across the Southeast. The most vulnerable sit in the Southwest deserts, the Great Plains and southern New England.
paras.zh: 一项为期四年的评估对下游 48 条河流和溪流在变暖气候下维持水生生物的能力进行了评级。最健康的地区集中在太平洋沿岸、落基山脉北部和整个东南部。最脆弱的地区位于西南部沙漠、大平原和新英格兰南部。

paras.en: Rivers doing well on all four criteria — more than half of the mapped stream distances — came out as resilient. The rest score near average, and were classed as restorable, still functional but held back by a problem, such as runoff from a farm or an obstructing dam, that one intervention could solve.
paras.zh: 在所有四个标准上都表现良好的河流（超过一半的地图河流距离）显示出具有弹性。其余的得分接近平均水平，被归类为可恢复、仍能发挥作用，但受到问题阻碍，例如农场径流或阻塞水坝，只需一次干预即可解决。

paras.en: Together the two categories form what the authors call a freshwater resilient and connected network, a shopping list of what the country would need to look after to keep its freshwater life going. “A resilient system is one that gives species options and environments in which to adapt,” Khoury says.
paras.zh: 这两个类别共同构成了作者所说的淡水弹性和互联网络，这是该国需要照顾以保持淡水生命延续的购物清单。 “一个有弹性的系统能够为物种提供适应的选择和环境，”库里说。

paras.en: Dams leave the clearest mark on the country’s rivers, carving them into more than 9,000 separate pieces. The study maps where reconnecting rivers would pay off most. Among the long unbroken stretches within the resilient system are Oregon and California’s Klamath River, whose lower dams came out in the largest removal project in U.S. history, and the Delaware River, which runs free of barriers along its main stem from New York’s Catskill Mountains to the sea.
paras.zh: 水坝在该国的河流上留下了最清晰的印记，将河流切割成 9,000 多块独立的碎片。该研究绘制了重新连接河流最能带来回报的地区。弹性系统内长长的、不间断的河段包括俄勒冈州和加利福尼亚州的克拉马斯河（其下游水坝是在美国历史上最大的拆除项目中建成的）和特拉华河（其从纽约卡茨基尔山脉到大海的主干流没有任何障碍）。

paras.en: “I can see this being overlaid in the future, for example, with where dam licenses will expire, in order to find the most effective restoration opportunities,” says Rafael Schmitt, a hydrologist at the University of California, Santa Barbara who was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: 未参与这项工作的加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校水文学家拉斐尔·施密特 (Rafael Schmitt) 表示：“我可以看到，未来这些信息会与大坝许可证到期的地点重叠，以便找到最有效的恢复机会。”

paras.en: Unlike on land, the study found, a river’s health says almost nothing about whether anyone is looking after it. On land, the healthiest places tend to be the protected ones. In water, however, 13 percent of the country’s stream distances are in good shape with no real safeguards, roughly twice the 6 percent that is both healthy and protected.
paras.zh: 研究发现，与陆地不同，河流的健康状况几乎不能说明是否有人在照顾它。在陆地上，最健康的地方往往是受保护的地方。然而，在水域方面，该国 13% 的河流状况良好，没有真正的保障措施，大约是健康且受保护的 6% 的两倍。

paras.en: The unprotected healthy rivers are the ones most at risk of slipping, because nothing keeps them in that condition. Locking in protection is harder for a river than for a forest. A designated preserve can hold a kilometer of stream while the water arriving in it may drain 100 kilometers of farm fields, dams and subdivisions. “It matters what’s going on upstream of that protected area,” Khoury says.
paras.zh: 未受保护的健康河流是最有可能发生滑坡的河流，因为没有任何东西可以使它们保持这种状态。河流的锁定保护比森林更难。一个指定的保护区可以容纳一公里长的溪流，而流入其中的水可能会排干 100 公里长的农田、水坝和小区。 “保护区上游发生的事情很重要，”库里说。

articles.title: A few drops of this Japanese tree oil may help you sleep more soundly

paras.en: A few drops of this Japanese tree oil may help you sleep more soundly
paras.zh: 几滴这种日本树油可以帮助您睡得更香

paras.en: A Japanese cypress root oil may help people wake less at night, fall into deeper sleep more smoothly, and feel more refreshed in the morning.
paras.zh: 日本丝柏根油可以帮助人们减少夜间醒来的次数，更顺利地进入更深的睡眠，并在早上感觉更精神焕发。

paras.en: - In a small study, sleeping near the scent of Hinoki root essential oil was linked to fewer nighttime awakenings, better morning alertness, and brain-wave changes associated with smoother sleep onset. The findings suggest an overlooked forestry byproduct could someday become a natural ingredient in sleep and relaxation products.
paras.zh: - 在一项小型研究中，在扁柏根精油的气味附近睡觉与夜间醒来次数减少、早晨警觉性提高以及与更平稳的入睡相关的脑电波变化有关。研究结果表明，一种被忽视的林业副产品有一天可能成为睡眠和放松产品的天然成分。

paras.en: Sleep difficulties are especially common during middle age, including among women in their 40s and 50s. New research suggests that an aromatic oil made from the roots of Hinoki (Chamaecyparis obtusa), also known as Japanese cypress, could offer a simple way to support better sleep at home.
paras.zh: 睡眠困难在中年时期尤其常见，包括 40 多岁和 50 多岁的女性。新的研究表明，由扁柏（Chamaecyparis obtusa）（也称为日本丝柏）根制成的芳香油可以提供一种简单的方法来支持在家中获得更好的睡眠。

paras.en: In a study published September 1, 2026, in the Journal of Wood Science, researchers tested Hinoki root essential oil and found several encouraging signs. Participants experienced fewer awakenings during the night, reported feeling better in the morning, and showed brain wave patterns associated with a smoother transition into sleep.
paras.zh: 在 2026 年 9 月 1 日发表在《木材科学杂志》上的一项研究中，研究人员测试了扁柏根精油，发现了一些令人鼓舞的迹象。参与者在夜间醒来的次数较少，早上感觉更好，并表现出与更平稳地进入睡眠状态相关的脑电波模式。

paras.en: Hinoki is an important timber tree in Japan, but its roots are often left behind and unused after logging. Those roots contain fragrant compounds that can be extracted to make essential oils.
paras.zh: 扁柏是日本重要的用材树种，但其根部在砍伐后经常被留下而未使用。这些根含有芳香化合物，可以提取制成精油。

paras.en: Scientists have previously investigated oils produced from Hinoki leaves and branches, but oils derived specifically from the roots have received far less attention.
paras.zh: 科学家此前曾研究过从扁柏树叶和树枝中提取的油，但专门从根部提取的油却受到的关注要少得多。

paras.en: "We wanted to address two questions: whether essential oil production could add value to underused Hinoki roots and whether that oil could improve sleep," says Associate Professor Kuniyoshi Shimizu from Kyushu University's Faculty of Agriculture. "In our earlier work, we examined sleep quality over a single day in a laboratory-like setting. However, sleep is strongly influenced by daily routines and the home environment. Therefore, we decided to examine the effect of repeated use over two weeks in participants' own bedrooms using both subjective assessments and physiological measurements."
paras.zh: “我们想解决两个问题：精油生产是否可以为未充分利用的扁柏根增加价值，以及精油是否可以改善睡眠，”九州大学农学院副教授清水国芳 (Kuniyoshi Shimizu) 说。 “在我们早期的工作中，我们在类似实验室的环境中检查了一天的睡眠质量。然而，睡眠受到日常生活和家庭环境的强烈影响。因此，我们决定使用主观评估和生理测量来检查在参与者自己的卧室中重复使用两周以上的效果。”

paras.en: The study involved 12 Japanese women between the ages of 35 and 60. Using a single blind crossover design, every participant spent two weeks using Hinoki root essential oil and another two weeks using an unscented control.
paras.zh: 该研究涉及 12 名年龄在 35 岁至 60 岁之间的日本女性。采用单盲交叉设计，每位参与者使用扁柏根精油两周，并另外两周使用无香对照。

paras.en: Before going to sleep, the women placed three drops of oil into a paper cup and breathed in the scent for 10 seconds. They then positioned the cup about 30 cm from their noses and left it there overnight.
paras.zh: 临睡前，妇女们将三滴油放入纸杯中，并吸入香味 10 秒钟。然后，他们将杯子放置在距离鼻子约 30 厘米的地方，并放置过夜。

paras.en: Researchers tracked sleep in several ways. Participants wore a headband that recorded brain waves, used a smartwatch to monitor sleep, and filled out a questionnaire each morning about how they had slept and how they felt upon waking.
paras.zh: 研究人员通过多种方式追踪睡眠。参与者戴着记录脑电波的头带，使用智能手表监测睡眠，并每天早上填写一份调查问卷，了解他们的睡眠情况以及醒来后的感受。

paras.en: Repeated exposure to the Hinoki root aroma was associated with improvements across several measures of sleep.
paras.zh: 反复接触扁柏根香气与多项睡眠指标的改善有关。

paras.en: By the 13th day of using the oil, participants said they felt less sleepy after waking and more recovered from fatigue compared with periods when they used the unscented control. Data from their smartwatches also indicated that they woke up fewer times during the night.
paras.zh: 在使用该油的第 13 天，参与者表示，与使用无味对照油的时期相比，他们醒来后感觉不那么困了，并且从疲劳中恢复得更好。来自他们智能手表的数据还表明，他们夜间醒来的次数较少。

paras.en: The brain wave recordings revealed another potentially important change. After seven days of using the Hinoki oil, participants showed increased delta wave activity around the time they were falling asleep. This pattern is consistent with a smoother progression into deeper stages of sleep.
paras.zh: 脑电波记录揭示了另一个潜在的重要变化。使用扁柏油 7 天后，参与者在入睡时表现出 δ 波活动增加。这种模式与更顺利地进入更深层次的睡眠阶段是一致的。

paras.en: Participants also responded positively to the scent itself. Compared with the control, they described the Hinoki aroma as more relaxing, comfortable, likable, elegant, nostalgic, and woody.
paras.zh: 参与者也对气味本身做出了积极的反应。与对照相比，他们形容扁柏香气更轻松、舒适、讨人喜欢、优雅、怀旧、木香。

paras.en: "By combining physiological measurements with participants' subjective assessments, we were able to examine sleep from multiple perspectives under everyday home conditions, which was an important aspect of this study," emphasizes Shimizu. "Our findings suggest that repeated use of Hinoki root essential oil at home may support sleep initiation, sleep continuity, and feeling refreshed in the morning."
paras.zh: “通过将生理测量与参与者的主观评估相结合，我们能够从多个角度检查日常家庭条件下的睡眠，这是这项研究的一个重要方面，”清水强调。 “我们的研究结果表明，在家中反复使用扁柏根精油可能有助于睡眠启动、睡眠连续性和早晨感觉神清气爽。”

paras.en: From Forestry Waste to a Potential Sleep Product
paras.zh: 从林业废物到潜在的睡眠产品

paras.en: The findings could eventually lead to aroma products made from Hinoki roots for bedrooms and other spaces intended for relaxation.
paras.zh: 这些发现最终可能会导致由扁柏根制成的芳香产品用于卧室和其他放松空间。

paras.en: The study also used an unusually simple setup. Participants only needed to place a small amount of essential oil near their beds. That approach could serve as a practical way to study other aromatic materials under normal home conditions rather than relying entirely on laboratory experiments.
paras.zh: 该研究还使用了异常简单的设置。参与者只需在床边放置少量精油即可。这种方法可以作为在正常家庭条件下研究其他芳香材料的实用方法，而不是完全依赖实验室实验。

paras.en: There could also be environmental and economic benefits. Turning Hinoki roots into useful aroma products may provide a higher value use for material that is commonly left behind after timber harvesting. The same idea could potentially be applied to other forestry residues that currently go underused.
paras.zh: 还可能带来环境和经济效益。将扁柏根转化为有用的芳香产品可以为木材采伐后通常留下的材料提供更高的价值。同样的想法也可能适用于目前未得到充分利用的其他林业残留物。

paras.en: Because the study was small, more research will be needed to determine which products work best, what doses are appropriate, and how the oil should be used for the most consistent results.
paras.zh: 由于研究规模较小，因此需要更多的研究来确定哪些产品效果最好、剂量合适以及如何使用油才能获得最一致的结果。

paras.en: Materials provided by Kyushu University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 资料由九州大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Fadilla Zennifa, Akiko Isa, Erika Tomimatsu, Yanli Xu, Ryuma Taki, Hiroo Yasutomi, Naotoshi Yasumori, Kuniyoshi Shimizu. Sleep improvement by Kagawa Hinoki root volatiles in middle-aged women: a home-based pilot study. Journal of Wood Science, 2026; DOI: 10.1186/s10086-026-02296-3
paras.zh: - Fadilla Zennifa、Akiko Isa、Erika Tomimatsu、Yanli Xu、Ryuma Taki、Hiroo Yasutomi、Naotoshi Yasumori、Kuniyoshi Shimizu。香川扁柏根挥发物改善中年女性的睡眠：一项以家庭为基础的试点研究。木材科学杂志，2026； DOI：10.1186/s10086-026-02296-3

articles.title: Scientists finally see how nature moves energy so efficiently

paras.en: Scientists finally see how nature moves energy so efficiently
paras.zh: 科学家终于看到大自然如何如此有效地转移能量

paras.en: - Researchers have captured key steps in a chemical reaction that helps nature transfer energy with remarkable efficiency. Ultrafast X-rays revealed how changes involving electrons and protons are closely linked to the rearrangement of surrounding water molecules. Because similar reactions drive photosynthesis and other energy-conversion processes, the technique could help scientists develop better catalysts, fuel cells, and flow batteries.
paras.zh: - 研究人员捕获了化学反应的关键步骤，帮助大自然以惊人的效率转移能量。超快 X 射线揭示了电子和质子的变化如何与周围水分子的重新排列密切相关。由于类似的反应驱动光合作用和其他能量转换过程，该技术可以帮助科学家开发更好的催化剂、燃料电池和液流电池。

paras.en: Some of the most important reactions in nature depend on positively and negatively charged particles moving in a coordinated way. These reactions are essential to processes such as photosynthesis, catalysis and biological energy conversion, but they happen so quickly that they are extremely difficult to observe.
paras.zh: 自然界中一些最重要的反应取决于带正电和带负电的粒子以协调的方式运动。这些反应对于光合作用、催化和生物能量转换等过程至关重要，但它们发生得如此之快，以至于极难观察到。

paras.en: A team led by the Department of Energy's Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, working with researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory and several universities, has now captured snapshots of these events after they are triggered by light striking a molecule.
paras.zh: 由能源部太平洋西北国家实验室领导的一个团队与 SLAC 国家加速器实验室和几所大学的研究人员合作，现已捕捉到这些由光撞击分子触发的事件的快照。

paras.en: The findings, published in Nature Communications, could deepen scientists' understanding of these reactions and eventually contribute to improved flow batteries, fuel cells and catalysts.
paras.zh: 该研究结果发表在《自然通讯》上，可以加深科学家对这些反应的理解，并最终有助于改进液流电池、燃料电池和催化剂。

paras.en: At the center of the study is the coordinated motion of positively charged protons and negatively charged electrons. This type of energy transfer is among the most efficient known in nature. Plants use related processes to capture energy from sunlight and convert it into stored chemical energy.
paras.zh: 这项研究的核心是带正电的质子和带负电的电子的协调运动。这种类型的能量转移是自然界已知的最有效的能量转移类型之一。植物利用相关过程从阳光中捕获能量并将其转化为储存的化学能。

paras.en: When electrons and protons move in a coordinated way, molecules can avoid intermediate steps that would otherwise require more energy. That can make a reaction both faster and much more efficient. The researchers investigated how changes in a molecule's electronic structure, the arrival of a proton and shifts in the surrounding water environment are connected during this process.
paras.zh: 当电子和质子以协调的方式移动时，分子可以避免需要更多能量的中间步骤。这可以使反应更快、更有效。研究人员研究了在此过程中分子电子结构的变化、质子的到达以及周围水环境的变化如何相互关联。

paras.en: Capturing a Reaction at the Molecular Level
paras.zh: 捕获分子水平的反应

paras.en: Scientists have studied this interaction for decades, but no previous experiment had captured the process in a single study with both local and structural sensitivity. Advanced X-ray techniques at the Linac Coherent Light Source at SLAC, combined with state-of-the-art quantum chemistry calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, provided an unusually detailed view.
paras.zh: 科学家们对这种相互作用进行了数十年的研究，但之前没有任何实验能够在一项具有局部和结构敏感性的研究中捕获这一过程。 SLAC 直线加速器相干光源的先进 X 射线技术与最先进的量子化学计算和分子动力学模拟相结合，提供了异常详细的视图。

paras.en: PNNL experimental chemical physicist Elisa Biasin, former PNNL scientist Abdullah Kahraman and PNNL theorists Niranjan (Niri) Govind and Amity Andersen worked with collaborators to study a light-driven proton-coupled electron transfer reaction, or PCET.
paras.zh: PNNL 实验化学物理学家 Elisa Biasin、前 PNNL 科学家 Abdullah Kahraman 以及 PNNL 理论家 Niranjan (Niri) Govind 和 Amity Andersen 与合作者合作研究光驱动质子耦合电子转移反应 (PCET)。

paras.en: The team combined ultrafast X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray scattering and advanced simulations to capture important stages of the reaction. For the first time with structural sensitivity, the researchers were able to show how a molecule's electronic structure changes at specific locations as it gains a proton, while the surrounding water environment reorganizes at the same time.
paras.zh: 该团队结合了超快 X 射线光谱、X 射线散射和先进的模拟来捕捉反应的重要阶段。研究人员首次凭借结构敏感性，展示了分子在获得质子时特定位置的电子结构如何变化，而周围的水环境同时重组。

paras.en: "We have captured for the first time how electronic changes associated with proton transfer are coupled to reorganization of the surrounding solvent," said Biasin. "This gives us a new way to understand how molecules and their environments evolve together during fundamental chemical transformations."
paras.zh: “我们首次捕获了与质子转移相关的电子变化如何与周围溶剂的重组相结合，”比亚辛说。 “这为我们提供了一种新的方法来理解分子及其环境在基本化学转变过程中如何共同进化。”

paras.en: Why Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Matters
paras.zh: 为什么质子耦合电子转移很重要

paras.en: PCET plays an important role throughout nature. Plants rely on it during photosynthesis to harvest light, while animals use related processes to efficiently convert food into energy. It is also involved in many other forms of biological and chemical energy conversion.
paras.zh: PCET 在自然界中发挥着重要作用。植物在光合作用过程中依靠它来获取光线，而动物则利用相关过程将食物有效地转化为能量。它还涉及许多其他形式的生物和化学能量转换。

paras.en: For the particular experimental system examined in this study, researchers already understand the basic mechanism. But many questions remain about other PCET reactions, especially the precise timing and order in which electrons and protons move.
paras.zh: 对于本研究中检查的特定实验系统，研究人员已经了解其基本机制。但其他 PCET 反应仍然存在许多问题，尤其是电子和质子移动的精确时间和顺序。

paras.en: "Are they happening together or not? At which molecular site? And how is the water network facilitating the proton hop?" Biasin asked. "These are some of the possible open questions. To answer them, you need ultra-fast time resolution, chemical and structural sensitivity, and alignment with theory. We have made a step forward to shed light on these questions."
paras.zh: “它们是否同时发生？在哪个分子位点？水网络如何促进质子跳跃？”比亚辛问道。 “这些是一些可能存在的开放性问题。要回答这些问题，你需要超快的时间分辨率、化学和结构敏感性以及与理论的一致性。我们已经在阐明这些问题上迈出了一步。”

paras.en: The new method gives researchers a way to investigate those questions more directly. The results show that local changes in electronic structure occur alongside a broader rearrangement of the surrounding water network as the molecule gains a proton.
paras.zh: 新方法为研究人员提供了一种更直接地调查这些问题的方法。结果表明，当分子获得质子时，电子结构的局部变化与周围水网络的更广泛的重新排列一起发生。

paras.en: Being able to examine these connected changes could eventually help researchers design more efficient catalysts, fuel cells, flow batteries and other technologies for converting and storing energy.
paras.zh: 能够检查这些相互关联的变化最终可以帮助研究人员设计更高效的催化剂、燃料电池、液流电池和其他用于转换和存储能量的技术。

paras.en: One major challenge is speed. Electrons move on extremely short timescales, and protons move nearly as fast. At the same time, water molecules surrounding the reacting molecules constantly shift and reorganize in ways that are notoriously difficult to observe directly.
paras.zh: 其中一项主要挑战是速度。电子在极短的时间尺度上移动，而质子的移动速度几乎同样快。与此同时，反应分子周围的水分子不断地以难以直接观察的方式移动和重组。

paras.en: Previous experiments could capture individual parts of this process, but they could not provide a combined picture of both the electronic changes inside the molecule and the reorganization occurring around it.
paras.zh: 以前的实验可以捕获该过程的各个部分，但无法提供分子内部电子变化及其周围发生的重组的综合图像。

paras.en: To create a system that would be easier to interpret, Biasin and her colleagues selected a well-studied ruthenium-based molecule. The molecule absorbs light and, in acidic conditions, captures a proton from its surroundings.
paras.zh: 为了创建一个更容易解释的系统，比亚辛和她的同事选择了一种经过充分研究的钌基分子。该分子吸收光，并在酸性条件下从周围环境中捕获质子。

paras.en: "We identified the metal complex used in this study because it does not undergo additional electronic and structural rearrangements that complicate interpretation of X-ray signals, allowing us to isolate signals associated with the electron, proton and solvent motion," said Christopher Larsen, a co-investigator and senior lecturer at the University of Aukland, New Zealand.
paras.zh: 新西兰奥克兰大学的联合研究员兼高级讲师克里斯托弗·拉森 (Christopher Larsen) 表示：“我们确定了本研究中使用的金属配合物，因为它不会发生额外的电子和结构重排，从而使 X 射线信号的解释变得复杂，从而使我们能够分离与电子、质子和溶剂运动相关的信号。”

paras.en: The researchers next used time-resolved characterization methods at the University of Geneva to identify the best experimental conditions and timescales for the X-ray measurements.
paras.zh: 研究人员接下来在日内瓦大学使用时间分辨表征方法来确定 X 射线测量的最佳实验条件和时间尺度。

paras.en: Combining X-Ray Techniques With Simulations
paras.zh: 将 X 射线技术与模拟相结合

paras.en: To track what happened during the reaction, the team combined two complementary X-ray methods.
paras.zh: 为了追踪反应过程中发生的情况，该团队结合了两种互补的 X 射线方法。

paras.en: Element-specific X-ray absorption spectroscopy using the chemRIXS instrument showed how electrons moved between different molecular sites. Meanwhile, time-resolved X-ray scattering from the X-ray Correlation Spectroscopy (XCS) instrument tracked how atoms rearranged, including the motion of solvent molecules around the reaction.
paras.zh: 使用 chemRIXS 仪器进行的元素特异性 X 射线吸收光谱显示电子如何在不同分子位点之间移动。与此同时，X 射线相关光谱 (XCS) 仪器的时间分辨 X 射线散射跟踪原子如何重新排列，包括反应周围溶剂分子的运动。

paras.en: The team also relied heavily on theoretical modeling. Govind and Andersen contributed time-dependent density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations, respectively. Those calculations were critical for interpreting the complex X-ray signals and uncovering the underlying behavior of the electrons and protons.
paras.zh: 该团队还严重依赖理论模型。 Govind 和 Andersen 分别贡献了瞬态密度泛函理论和分子动力学模拟。这些计算对于解释复杂的 X 射线信号和揭示电子和质子的潜在行为至关重要。

paras.en: First author Abdullah Kahraman said the combination of methods was essential.
paras.zh: 第一作者阿卜杜拉·卡赫拉曼表示，多种方法的结合至关重要。

paras.en: "Understanding the photochemistry of this complex required us to push the limits of our data analysis. By combining X-ray absorption spectroscopy with precise theoretical modeling, we gained an unprecedented look into the real-time electronic changes driving these reactions," said Kahraman, who worked on the project at SLAC while he was a PNNL postdoctoral associate.
paras.zh: “了解这种复合体的光化学需要我们突破数据分析的极限。通过将 X 射线吸收光谱与精确的理论模型相结合，我们对驱动这些反应的实时电子变化有了前所未有的了解，”卡赫拉曼说，他在担任 PNNL 博士后助理时曾在 SLAC 参与该项目。

paras.en: Govind highlighted the theoretical aspect of the research.
paras.zh: 戈文德强调了该研究的理论方面。

paras.en: "While this was an experiment-driven discovery, our theoretical work provided the molecular-level interpretation needed to translate the X-ray measurements into a detailed picture of the underlying coordination between proton, electron and solvent motion."
paras.zh: “虽然这是一个实验驱动的发现，但我们的理论工作提供了分子水平的解释，将 X 射线测量结果转化为质子、电子和溶剂运动之间潜在协调的详细图片。”

paras.en: Biasin noted that the experiment could not directly observe the proton itself.
paras.zh: 比亚辛指出，该实验无法直接观察质子本身。

paras.en: "X-ray scattering mostly sees atoms that are rich with electrons, and so the proton is not seen directly," she said. "But we observe the local reorganization of the electronic structure, together with the global reorganization of the water networks, and we can draw conclusions based on the agreement between data and calculations."
paras.zh: “X射线散射主要看到富含电子的原子，因此不能直接看到质子，”她说。 “但我们观察电子结构的局部重组，以及水网络的全局重组，我们可以根据数据和计算之间的一致性得出结论。”

paras.en: Even with that limitation, the combined X-ray approach provides a framework that researchers can now apply to PCET reactions in more complicated chemical systems.
paras.zh: 即使存在这种限制，组合的 X 射线方法也提供了一个框架，研究人员现在可以将其应用于更复杂的化学系统中的 PCET 反应。

paras.en: "Many of the most important chemical reactions involve electrons, protons, and their surrounding environment moving together on ultrafast timescales," said Roberto Alonso Mori, senior scientist at SLAC and a coauthor on the study. "By combining complementary X-ray techniques at LCLS, this work provides a uniquely complete view of these coupled processes, opening new opportunities to understand and ultimately control the chemistry that underpins energy conversion and catalysis."
paras.zh: SLAC 高级科学家、该研究的合著者罗伯托·阿隆索·莫里 (Roberto Alonso Mori) 表示：“许多最重要的化学反应都涉及电子、质子及其周围环境在超快时间尺度上一起移动。” “通过结合 LCLS 的互补 X 射线技术，这项工作提供了这些耦合过程的独特完整视图，为理解并最终控制支撑能量转换和催化的化学物质提供了新的机会。”

paras.en: Coauthor and SLAC staff scientist David Hoffman added, "This is an important first step in combining X-ray scattering and spectroscopy to study these complicated processes in a model system. With the better signal-to-noise offered by the LCLS-II upgrade, we can use these methods to solve real problems in catalysis and energy harvesting."
paras.zh: 合著者、SLAC 科学家 David Hoffman 补充道：“这是将 X 射线散射和光谱学结合起来研究模型系统中这些复杂过程的重要的第一步。凭借 LCLS-II 升级提供的更好的信噪比，我们可以使用这些方法来解决催化和能量收集中的实际问题。”

paras.en: The research was supported by the DOE Office of Science, Basic Energy Sciences, Chemical Sciences, Geosciences, and Biosciences Division, through the Condensed Phase and Interfacial Molecular Science (CPIMS) program and the Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Sciences (AMOS) program at PNNL.
paras.zh: 该研究得到了美国能源部科学、基础能源科学、化学科学、地球科学和生物科学部办公室通过凝相和界面分子科学 (CPIMS) 项目以及 PNNL 原子、分子和光学科学 (AMOS) 项目的支持。

paras.en: Use of the Linac Coherent Light Source at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory is supported by the DOE Office of Science. Part of the research was also conducted at the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a DOE Office of Science user facility located at PNNL.
paras.zh: SLAC 国家加速器实验室使用直线加速器相干光源得到了美国能源部科学办公室的支持。部分研究还在环境分子科学实验室进行，该实验室是位于 PNNL 的美国能源部科学办公室用户设施。

paras.en: Materials provided by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. Original written by Karyn Hede. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由太平洋西北国家实验室提供。原创作者：Karyn Hede。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: One simple addition to postpartum care made a major difference

paras.en: One simple addition to postpartum care made a major difference
paras.zh: 产后护理的一个简单补充就产生了重大影响

paras.en: Patient navigators helped new mothers overcome healthcare barriers and stay connected to critical postpartum and primary care long after giving birth.
paras.zh: 患者导航器帮助新妈妈们克服医疗保健障碍，并在产后很长一段时间内与重要的产后和初级保健保持联系。

paras.en: - New mothers paired with patient navigators were much more likely to receive postpartum care, depression screening, preventive testing, and ongoing primary care. By helping with barriers such as transportation, childcare, scheduling, and confusing medical information, navigators may provide a powerful way to improve womenâs long-term health.
paras.zh: - 与患者导航员配对的新妈妈更有可能接受产后护理、抑郁症筛查、预防性测试和持续的初级护理。通过帮助克服交通、儿童保育、日程安排和混乱的医疗信息等障碍，导航器可能会提供一种改善女性长期健康的有力方法。

paras.en: Becoming a mother can be difficult under any circumstances, but for some women, everyday obstacles can make getting medical care after childbirth especially challenging. Limited health literacy, unreliable transportation, difficulty navigating a complicated healthcare system, lack of childcare, and unstable housing can all determine whether a new mother receives needed care or goes without it.
paras.zh: 在任何情况下，成为母亲都可能很困难，但对于一些女性来说，日常障碍可能会让产后获得医疗护理变得尤其困难。健康素养有限、交通不可靠、复杂的医疗保健系统难以驾驭、缺乏托儿服务以及不稳定的住房都可能决定新妈妈是否得到所需的护理。

paras.en: New research from Northwestern Medicine suggests that patient navigators can help remove many of those barriers. These trained guides work with patients and healthcare teams to connect people with medical care, services, and other resources. Among low-income pregnant individuals, the approach was linked to better postpartum health care and stronger connections to primary care that continued well beyond childbirth.
paras.zh: 西北医学的新研究表明，患者导航器可以帮助消除其中许多障碍。这些训练有素的指南与患者和医疗团队合作，将人们与医疗护理、服务和其他资源联系起来。在低收入孕妇中，这种方法与更好的产后医疗保健和与初级保健的更牢固的联系有关，这种联系在分娩后仍持续很长时间。

paras.en: The study was published Oct. 2 in JAMA Health Forum. According to the researchers, it is among the first studies to describe what an ideal model of postpartum care in the U.S. could look like.
paras.zh: 该研究于 10 月 2 日发表在《JAMA 健康论坛》上。研究人员表示，这是最早描述美国理想产后护理模式的研究之一。

paras.en: Patient Navigators Improved Postpartum Care
paras.zh: 患者导航器改善产后护理

paras.en: Compared with patients who received usual postpartum care without a patient navigator, those who worked with a navigator were more likely to:
paras.zh: 与在没有患者导航仪的情况下接受常规产后护理的患者相比，使用导航仪的患者更有可能：

paras.en: - Attend postpartum care visits (96% vs. 80% among those receiving usual postpartum care without a patient navigator)
paras.zh: - 参加产后护理就诊（在没有患者导航仪的情况下接受常规产后护理的患者中，这一比例为 96% 对比 80%）

paras.en: - Be counseled about all needed postpartum topics (65% vs. 51%)
paras.zh: - 获得有关所有需要的产后主题的咨询（65% 与 51%）

paras.en: - Have screening and care for postpartum depression (86% vs. 72%) in the critical "fourth trimester" months
paras.zh: - 在关键的“妊娠第四期”月份对产后抑郁症进行筛查和护理（86% 对比 72%）

paras.en: - Attend a primary care visit (57% vs. 30%) at one year after giving birth
paras.zh: - 产后一年参加初级保健就诊（57% vs. 30%）

paras.en: - Be using their desired family planning method, such as birth control, at one year to help space out their pregnancies (65% vs. 43%)
paras.zh: - 在一年内使用他们想要的计划生育方法，例如节育，以帮助间隔怀孕时间（65% vs. 43%）

paras.en: - Receive preventive health testing (i.e. blood pressure (85% vs 62%), lipids (28% vs 13%) and glucose (31% vs 16%)
paras.zh: - 接受预防性健康测试（即血压（85% vs 62%）、血脂（28% vs 13%）和血糖（31% vs 16%）

paras.en: "Pregnancy and the postpartum periods are complex, and people often deprioritize themselves, particularly if they don't have much support or have complex social needs," said corresponding author Dr. Lynn Yee, chief of maternal-fetal medicine in the department of obstetrics and gynecology at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and a Northwestern Medicine physician. "Combined with a fragmented healthcare system, many people do not receive the care they need."
paras.zh: “怀孕和产后时期很复杂，人们常常会降低自己的优先级，特别是当他们没有太多支持或有复杂的社会需求时，”通讯作者、西北大学范伯格医学院妇产科母胎医学主任、西北医学医师 Lynn Yee 博士说。 “再加上分散的医疗保健系统，许多人没有得到他们需要的护理。”

paras.en: "That makes a perfect storm of suboptimal women's health in this very key postpartum period, which is when we know many women drop out of care. If we can address this gap early and sustain their engagement with healthcare, we can make a difference in the health and well-being of women over the long run."
paras.zh: “在这个非常关键的产后时期，这使得女性的健康状况不佳，这是一场完美的风暴，我们知道很多女性在这个时期放弃了护理。如果我们能够及早解决这一差距并维持她们对医疗保健的参与，从长远来看，我们可以为女性的健康和福祉带来改变。”

paras.en: Patient navigation is already widely used in cancer care and is even funded by Medicaid, Yee said. However, the approach has received far less attention in postpartum care and has remained both understudied and underused.
paras.zh: Yee 说，患者导航已经广泛应用于癌症护理，甚至得到了医疗补助的资助。然而，该方法在产后护理中受到的关注要少得多，并且仍然没有得到充分研究和利用。

paras.en: The researchers said this is the first large-scale study to investigate the benefits of patient navigation among pregnant and postpartum individuals. The results could provide a foundation for additional research and potentially support future funding for postpartum navigation programs.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，这是第一项调查孕妇和产后个体导航的好处的大规模研究。研究结果可以为进一步的研究奠定基础，并有可能为未来的产后导航项目提供资金支持。

paras.en: How Patient Navigators Helped New Mothers
paras.zh: 耐心导航员如何帮助新妈妈

paras.en: The study included 405 pregnant individuals receiving care at Prentice Women's Hospital in Chicago between 2020 and 2024. Participants assigned a patient navigator began working with that person near the end of pregnancy and continued receiving support throughout the first year after delivery.
paras.zh: 该研究纳入了 2020 年至 2024 年间在芝加哥 Prentice 妇女医院接受护理的 405 名孕妇。参与者指定一名患者导航员，在怀孕快结束时开始与该人一起工作，并在分娩后的第一年继续接受支持。

paras.en: The navigators spoke both English and Spanish and worked closely with patients to develop postpartum care plans, which were also shared with the medical team. They scheduled and attended appointments, helped coordinate transportation and childcare, communicated with doctors and nurses, and helped patients make sense of complicated medical information. They also worked to strengthen health literacy and give patients greater confidence in managing their own care.
paras.zh: 导航员会讲英语和西班牙语，并与患者密切合作制定产后护理计划，并与医疗团队分享。他们安排和参加预约，帮助协调交通和儿童保育，与医生和护士沟通，并帮助患者理解复杂的医疗信息。他们还努力加强健康素养，让患者更有信心管理自己的护理。

paras.en: The transition from pregnancy care to primary care can have important long-term consequences. Previous research has shown that complications such as gestational diabetes and preeclampsia can affect health years later, making continued medical follow-up especially important.
paras.zh: 从妊娠护理到初级护理的转变可能会产生重要的长期后果。先前的研究表明，妊娠糖尿病和先兆子痫等并发症可能会在数年后影响健康，因此持续的医疗随访尤为重要。

paras.en: Even people who have healthy pregnancies can encounter serious challenges after delivery. Postpartum depression, limited partner support, housing problems, domestic violence, and other unmet social or safety needs can make it harder for new mothers to prioritize their own health, Yee said.
paras.zh: 即使怀孕健康的人在分娩后也会遇到严峻的挑战。伊说，产后抑郁症、有限的伴侣支持、住房问题、家庭暴力以及其他未满足的社会或安全需求可能会让新妈妈更难优先考虑自己的健康。

paras.en: The researchers said the program's success in connecting postpartum patients with primary care demonstrates how navigators may help close some of these gaps.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，该计划成功地将产后患者与初级保健联系起来，这表明导航器可以如何帮助缩小其中一些差距。

paras.en: "Cumulatively not engaging in health-promotion behaviors in the postpartum period has reverberating implications for the family unit, too," Yee said.
paras.zh: “在产后期间不参与促进健康的行为对家庭单位也会产生影响，”Yee 说。

paras.en: The benefits were not limited to patients. The study found that healthcare professionals also valued the support provided by navigators.
paras.zh: 好处不仅限于患者。研究发现，医疗保健专业人员也重视导航员提供的支持。

paras.en: For example, if a patient was unable to attend an appointment, a navigator could notify the doctor, arrange a new appointment, or handle administrative tasks that might otherwise fall to clinical staff. Navigators also helped make sure patients completed important follow-up steps after appointments, including glucose tolerance testing and subsequent medical visits.
paras.zh: 例如，如果患者无法参加预约，导航员可以通知医生、安排新的预约或处理原本可能由临床工作人员承担的管理任务。导航器还帮助确保患者在预约后完成重要的后续步骤，包括葡萄糖耐量测试和随后的就诊。

paras.en: "One of the goals of navigators was not just to help patients, but to help clinicians too, and doctors were happy at how much more efficient and engaged patients were," said co-author Joseph Feinglass, research professor of general internal medicine at Feinberg.
paras.zh: “导航员的目标之一不仅是帮助患者，还帮助临床医生，医生们对患者的效率和参与度大大提高感到高兴，”合著者、范伯格普通内科研究教授约瑟夫·芬格拉斯 (Joseph Feinglass) 说。

paras.en: Before taking part in the study, patient navigator Viridiana Carmona-Barrera had worked in hospital, insurance and women's health settings. That background gave her experience with many of the obstacles pregnant patients can encounter.
paras.zh: 在参与这项研究之前，患者导航员 Viridiana Carmona-Barrera 曾在医院、保险公司和妇女健康机构工作。这种背景让她经历了怀孕患者可能遇到的许多障碍。

paras.en: She recalled helping one pregnant patient with chronic health conditions who was in danger of missing an important appointment because she lacked reliable transportation and childcare. After other attempts to reach a solution were unsuccessful, Carmona-Barrera coordinated both transportation and childcare so the patient could make the appointment.
paras.zh: 她回忆起帮助一名患有慢性疾病的孕妇的经历，她因缺乏可靠的交通和儿童保育而面临错过重要预约的危险。在其他尝试达成解决方案失败后，卡莫纳-巴雷拉协调了交通和儿童保育，以便患者可以预约。

paras.en: "I like being someone who can help make these processes easier," Carmona-Barrera said. "As committed as health care organizations are to supporting patients, navigating the system can still be challenging."
paras.zh: “我喜欢成为能够帮助简化这些过程的人，”卡莫纳-巴雷拉说。 “尽管医疗保健组织致力于支持患者，但驾驭该系统仍然具有挑战性。”

paras.en: An important goal of the program was not to make patients permanently dependent on navigators. Instead, the researchers wanted participants to become more comfortable interacting with the healthcare system and more capable of managing their own care.
paras.zh: 该计划的一个重要目标是不让患者永远依赖导航仪。相反，研究人员希望参与者能够更轻松地与医疗保健系统互动，并且更有能力管理自己的护理。

paras.en: By building those skills over the first year after childbirth, the team hoped patients would eventually feel confident arranging appointments, seeking primary care, and navigating the healthcare system without additional assistance.
paras.zh: 通过在产后第一年培养这些技能，该团队希望患者最终能够自信地安排预约、寻求初级保健以及在没有额外帮助的情况下使用医疗保健系统。

paras.en: "Their goal was to put themselves out of business, to be able to get to the end of the year and say, 'You don't need me anymore,'" Yee said. "That's success for a navigation program."
paras.zh: “他们的目标是让自己破产，以便能够到年底说，‘你不再需要我了，’”易说。 “这就是导航计划的成功。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Northwestern University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由西北大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

Grobman. Patient Navigation and Postpartum Health Care Outcomes. JAMA Health Forum, 2026; 7 (10): e263338 DOI: 10.1001/jamahealthforum.2026.3338
